The monomials in the elements

$\big\{s_{ij}^{(r)}\big\}_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0},1\leqslant j0},1\leqslant k\leqslant N}$

taken in any fixed linear order form a PBW basis of ${\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{+}$.

(2)

The monomials in the elements

$\displaystyle\big\{s_{2i-1,2i-1}^{(r)}\big\}_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0},\,1\leqslant i\leqslant N/2}$ $\displaystyle\cup\big\{s_{2i-1,2i}^{(2r-1)},\,s_{2i,2i-1}^{(2r-1)}\big\}_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0},\,1\leqslant i\leqslant N/2}$

$\cup\{s_{ij}^{(r)}\}_{r\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}, 1\leqslant j

taken in any fixed linear order form a PBW basis of ${\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{-}$.

It is well known that ${\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$ can be identified as a subalgebra of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{N})$. Specifically, the map

(2.16)

$S(u)\mapsto T^{t}(-u)GT(u)G^{-1}$

defines an embedding ${\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{N})$. Here $t$ stands for the regular transpose. Then there is a filtration, which we call the loop filtration again, on ${\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$ inherited from the one (2.4) on $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{N})$ such that $\deg s_{ij}^{(r)}=r-1$. Let $\mathcal{F}_{s}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$ be the subspace of ${\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$ spanned by elements of degree $\leqslant s$ such that

(2.17)

$\displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{0}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}\subset\mathcal{F}_{1}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}\subset\mathcal{F}_{2}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}\subset\ldots,\qquad\qquad{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}=\bigcup_{s\geqslant 0}\mathcal{F}_{s}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}.$

Denote by $\operatorname{gr}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$ the associated graded algebra. Let $\bar{s}_{ij}^{(r)}$ be the image of $s_{ij}^{(r)}$ in the $(r-1)$ -st component of $\operatorname{gr}{\mathscr{Y}}^{\pm}_{N}$.

Let $\theta$ be the involution of $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}$ defined by

(2.18)

$\displaystyle\theta:\mathfrak{gl}_{N}\longrightarrow\mathfrak{gl}_{N},\quad e_{ij}\mapsto-\theta_{i}\theta_{j}e_{j^{\prime}i^{\prime}}.$

Let $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}^{\theta}$ denote the fixed point subalgebra of $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}$ under $\theta$. For $1\leqslant i,j\leqslant N$, set

$f_{ij}:=e_{ij}-\theta_{i}\theta_{j}e_{j^{\prime}i^{\prime}}.$

Then $f_{j^{\prime}i^{\prime}}=-\theta_{i}\theta_{j}f_{ij}$ and $f_{ij}$ are elements in $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}^{\theta}$. Moreover, $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}^{\theta}$ is spanned by $f_{ij}$ and $\mathfrak{g}_{N}=\mathfrak{gl}_{N}^{\theta}$. It is well known that the twisted Yangians ${\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}$ have the evaluation homomorphism

(2.19)

$\xi^{\pm}:{\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}\to\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{g}_{N}),\qquad s_{ij}(u)\mapsto\delta_{ij}+(u+\tfrac{1}{2})^{-1}f_{ij}.$

In addition, the map $f_{ij}\mapsto s_{ij}^{(1)}$ defines an embedding of the algebra $\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{g}_{N})$ into ${\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm}$.

Extend $\theta$ to an involution on $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]$ (again denoted $\theta$ ) by sending $g\otimes z^{r}$ to $\theta(g)\otimes(-z)^{r}$ for $g\in\mathfrak{gl}_{N}$ and $r\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]^{\theta}$ be the fixed point subalgebra of $\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]$ under the involution $\theta$. Then it is well known that the map

$\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{gl}_{N}[z]^{\theta})\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}{\mathscr{Y}}_{N}^{\pm},\qquad e_{ij}\otimes z^{r}-(-1)^{r}\theta_{i}\theta_{j}e_{j^{\prime}i^{\prime}}\otimes z^{r}\mapsto\bar{s}_{ij}^{(r+1)}$

induces an algebra isomorphism.

The following result follows from (2.3) and (2.16).

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and finite $W$-algebras of classical type
paper.abstract: We introduce parabolic presentations of twisted Yangians of types AI and AII, interpolating between the R-matrix presentation and the Drinfeld presentation. Then we formulate and provide parabolic presentations for the shifted twisted Yangians. We define quotient algebras known as truncated shifted twisted Yangians and equip them with baby comultiplications, generalizing the work of Brundan and Kleshchev. PBW bases for all (truncated) shifted twisted Yangians of type AI and AII are established along the way. Applying the theory of universal equivariant quantizations of conic symplectic singularities we show that the truncated twisted shifted Yangian is isomorphic to the finite $W$-algebra which quantizes a suitable Slodowy slice. This provides a presentation of the finite $W$-algebra associated with every even nilpotent element in type {\sf B} and {\sf C}, as well as every nilpotent element with two Jordan blocks in type {\sf D}. Finally we make a conjecture which would supply presentations in the remaining even cases in type {\sf D}.
